title: Protocol for measuring BRAF autoinhibition in live cells using a proximity-based NanoBRET assay
protocol: Detach 293FT cells from tissue culture dish using trypsin-EDTA.
Incubate the 10 cm dish at 37°C for approximately 3–5 min or until cells begin to detach from the surface.
Add 9 ml of DMEM growth media directly to the trypsin-EDTA/cell mixture.
Pipette mixture up and down vigorously to generate a single-cell suspension.
Count and seed cells using trypan blue exclusion method.
Determine cell number using an automated cell counter or hemocytometer.
Dilute cell suspension to 2 × 10^5 cells/mL.
Plate 2 ml of the diluted cell suspension (4 × 10^5 cells) into each well of a 6-well tissue culture plate.
Seed cells in wells of the 6-well plates for planned assays.
Incubate plates at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 18 h to allow cells to recover and attach to well surface.
Dilute NanoBRET plasmids to 5 ng/μL.
Dilute pcDNA3.1 empty vector to 100 ng/μL.
Place 100 μL of serum-free Opti-MEM into each pre-labeled tube for assay conditions.
Add 20 ng of pCMV5-BRAFREG-Halo, 5 ng of pCMV5-Nano-BRAFCAT, and 200 ng of pcDNA3.1 empty vector directly into the Opti-MEM diluent.
Add 2 μL of X-tremeGENE 9 to each sample and vortex briefly to mix.
Pulse spin tubes in microfuge to remove any liquid that has accumulated in the lid.
Incubate tubes for 15 min at 20–25°C to allow transfection complexes to form.
Add transfection complexes dropwise to wells with attached cells.
Incubate plates at 37°C with 5% CO2 for at least 16 hours to allow expression of the exogenous proteins.
Include empty vector DNA (pcDNA3.1) in the transfection mix with NanoBRET DNA constructs.
Reduce the amount of empty vector DNA if other expression constructs are co-transfected.
Use high-purity plasmid DNAs for the assay to ensure sensitivity and consistency.
Include appropriate controls when first performing the assay or evaluating previously untested variants.
Co-express an activated KRAS mutant, such as G12V, as an external control for detecting a reduction in BRAF.
Replate cells into a 384-well white-walled tissue culture plate.
Transfer cells with or without the fluorescent NanoBRET HaloTag 618 ligand.
Replate remaining cells into fresh 6-well plates for western blot analysis.
Label three sets of sterile 1.7 mL tubes (Set 1–3) and one set of sterile 15 mL conical tubes for each sample.
Pre-warm trypsin-EDTA in a 37°C water bath.
Warm serum-free Opti-MEM (no phenol red) in a 37°C water bath.
Warm Opti-MEM containing 10% FBS in a 37°C water bath.
Pre-cool a low-speed centrifuge with a swinging bucket rotor to 4°C.
Collect cells from 6-well tissue culture plates.
Aspirate growth media from the wells containing cells.
Add 250 μl of trypsin-EDTA to each well.
Incubate plates at 37°C for 3–5 minutes or until cells begin to detach.
Add 1 ml of 10% FBS Opti-MEM (no phenol red) to each well.
Pipette vigorously to generate a single-cell suspension.
Transfer cells to a 15 ml conical tube.
Add 10% FBS Opti-MEM to make a total volume of 2 ml in the tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension in the 15 ml tubes at 200–300 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
During centrifugation, add 15 μl of trypan blue stain to the cell suspension in the 1.7 ml Set 1 tubes.
Count the cells as described above (a concentration of 6–8 × 10^5 cells/mL is typical).
Resuspend cell pellets in serum-free Opti-MEM.
Pipette vigorously to ensure a homogeneous single-cell suspension.
Invert 15 mL tubes several times to create a uniform cell suspension.
Pipette 500 μL of the cell suspension into sterile 1.7 mL Set 2 and Set 3 tubes.
Add 0.5 μL of Halo618 ligand into each Set 2 sample (+ ligand).
Add 0.5 μL of DMSO into each Set 3 sample (vehicle).
Mix samples thoroughly for both conditions.
Transfer cells in Set 2 (+ ligand) and Set 3 (vehicle) tubes to separate wells of a reagent reservoir.
Mix cell suspension thoroughly and plate into quadruplicate wells of a 384-well plate.
Plate vehicle (DMSO)-containing cell suspension in an identical manner.
Transfer remaining cell suspension from 15 mL tubes to individual wells of fresh 6-well tissue culture plates for western blot analysis.
Incubate plates at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 16 hours.
Mix NanoGlo substrate 1:100 in pre-warmed serum-free Opti-MEM.
Transfer the diluted NanoGlo substrate to a reagent reservoir.
Add 10 μL of the diluted NanoGlo substrate to cells in the 384-well plate.
Record NanoBRET emissions at 460 nm (donor) and 618 nm (acceptor).
Calculate corrected BRET ratio from recorded emissions.
Mix 10 μL of the substrate mix with each well of the 384 well plate that contains cells.
Shake the plate on an orbital shaker for 1 min at approximately 150 rpm.
Record donor (460 nm) and acceptor (618 nm) emissions within 10 min of substrate addition using a multi-label plate reader.
Calculate the BRET ratios for the vehicle and + ligand readings in milliBret Units (mBU).
Subtract the BRET ratio of the vehicle from the BRET ratio of the + ligand to calculate the corrected BRET ratio.
Lysate cells in the 6-well plates and normalize protein levels (1 h).
Add protease and phosphatase inhibitors to NP40 lysis buffer.
Aspirate media from 6-well plates.
Wash cells once with 1 mL of ice-cold PBS and aspirate.
Add 125 μL of NP40 lysis buffer to each well of cells.
Place the 6-well plates on a rocking platform at 4°C for 15 min.
Pre-cool a microcentrifuge to 4°C during Step 8e.
Label 2 sets of 1.7 mL tubes, placing Set 1 on ice.
Transfer lysates to Set 1 tubes.
Spin Set 1 tubes in the pre-cooled microfuge for 10 min at maximum speed of around 20,000 × g.
Place lysates on ice after spinning.
Determine protein concentration of each sample using commercially available assays such as Bradford Assay or BCA protein assay.
Transfer appropriate amount of lysate supernatant to the 1.7 mL Set 2 tubes, normalizing the protein content of the samples using NP40 lysis buffer to give a final volume of 100 μL.
Boil 5× protein sample buffer for 1 min and then add 25 μL to each sample.
Boil samples for 5–6 min.
Protein samples can now be stored at −80°C or separated by SDS-PAGE.
Run 25 μL of the protein samples on duplicate SDS-PAGE gels.
Transfer the separated proteins from the gels to nitrocellulose or PVDF membranes using a standard wet tank transfer system.
Block the membranes for 30 min at 20–25°C in a solution of 3% BSA in PBS.
Rinse membranes once with TBS (1×) containing 0.2% Tween20 (TBST).
Incubate the membranes for at least 16 h at 4°C with anti-Halo and Anti-NanoLuc antibodies diluted 1:1000 in TBST.
Wash the membranes three times in TBST for 5 min per wash the following day.
Incubate the membranes for 1 h at 20–25°C in anti-mouse HRP secondary antibody diluted 1:10,000 in TBST.
Wash membranes three times in TBST for 5 min per wash.
Visualize signals using ECL reagents, X-ray film, and a film processor or other ECL-compatible imaging systems.
Refer to troubleshooting 2 for possible solutions if non-equivalent expression levels of the REG and/or CAT domain proteins are observed.

Use more potent ECL reagents, such as Immobilon™ Western Chemiluminescent HRP Substrate (cat# WBKLS0500), or other western blot detection systems if required for visualizing low ng quantities of transfected plasmids.
